thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: shared GPU pool gpu-pool-4 reports sustained p99 streaming latency > 5s. trigger: p99_streaming_latency > 5s for 3m across clusters eu-west-1. paging oncall@eng-sre

irene: I'm taking the page. Pulling dashboards now — p95 ~ 820ms, p99 ~ 6.2s, streaming stall rate 4.8% (SLO breached). Top affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream

sam: any recent deploys to gpu-pool-4? i don't see any from release-bot in the last hour

vijay: no deploys. looks like a sudden IO tail. i can see a handful of tenants with heavy write throughput to local NVMe on nodes n-gpu-27 and n-gpu-29

luke: linking top queries by tenant, looks like tenant-hyper and tenant-ml-batch are spiking embedding jobs

irene: collecting per-node iostat and cgroup io stats. grabbing io.stat from container runtime

irene: paste: 
```
# sample io.stat excerpt
8:0 rbytes=1254389016 wbytes=981234123 rios=4121 wios=920
# kernel show: dm-crypt high latency and high write queue
```

sam: that matches kernel dmesg lines for n-gpu-29: blk_mq: dev sdb: increase request queue depth, blk dev busy

vijay: suspect noisy neighbor causing NVMe saturation -> streaming stalls since serving runtime waits on KV cache writes. suggested mitigations: apply cgroup io.max limits for offending containers OR migrate heavy tenants off gpu-pool-4 to dedicated-pool-2

luke: sysadmin note: we can set io.max via cgroup v2 with echo into /sys/fs/cgroup/<slice>/io.max. example command below, will need container id

irene: trying quick mitigation: identify top container id for tenant-hyper and apply conservative write limit 100MB/s

irene: running:
```
# find container
docker ps --filter label=tenant=tenant-hyper -q
# then
echo 8:0 rbps=0 wbps=104857600 > /sys/fs/cgroup/docker/<cid>/io.max
```

oncall-bot: action logged: cgroup io.max applied to container <cid> by irene at 1737504600

sam: i'm going to cordon node n-gpu-29 and evict non-critical pods to reduce pressure, will drain gradually

vijay: also starting live migration of tenant-hyper workload to dedicated-pool-2 via k8s controller: scale up dedicated pool, set nodeSelector, then rollout

luke: support-team, any customer complaints yet? need to track customer impact for incident report

support-team: we received two priority tickets from acme-corp and fastapps complaining about streaming timeouts. acme-corp error rate peaked at 6.4% on affected route. we've opened incident tickets P1-348 and P1-349 and contacted their SREs

irene: after applying io.max and starting migration, raw metrics update: p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 900ms in 90s, p95 steady ~820ms, streaming stalls down to 0.7%

sam: cordon/drain progress: n-gpu-29 drained 80%, currently evicting a long-running batch job via graceful termination

vijay: migration completed for tenant-hyper, validated traffic shift, no errors on dedicated pool

luke: any signs of residual IO pressure on n-gpu-27? it's still slightly elevated but within baseline. plan: leave io.max in place for next 30m then gradually relax

irene: agreed. i'm tagging this incident as mitigated. continuing to monitor for 30m. creating postmortem assign

oncall-bot: incident status updated: mitigated at 1737505140. monitoring window until 1737506940

support-team: notifying acme-corp contacts: provided RCA-in-progress note and ETA for postmortem. they acknowledged and will hold SLO credits discussion after RCA

vijay: root cause hypothesis: tenant-hyper started a large embedding write workflow that caused sustained NVMe write saturation on two colocated nodes; no cgroup io.limit existed prior to this run. failure mode cascaded to serving runtime via KV persistence stalls -> streaming stalls

sam: next actions: 1) create automatic cgroup io profile for heavy-io tenants 2) add alert for per-node nvme write saturation 3) recommend tenancy isolation thresholds and admission control to prevent colocating two heavy-io tenants on same nodes

irene: assigning postmortem owner: vijay. timeline notes and dumps saved to incident archive id pgn-1737504321

luke: i'm updating runbook with the temporary io.max commands + k8s migration steps we used. will add safer automated flow for future

oncall-bot: handoff scheduled: irene -> next oncall sam at 08:00 PST. handoff recorded

irene: handing off now. i've left buffers and the io.max applied to offending container for rollback. will remove limits only after 30m stable window. thanks everyone

support-team: final customer update posted to P1 tickets. will follow up after postmortem

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - mitigations successful and service returned to SLO. resolution at 1737505400. postmortem assigned to vijay. tags: noisy-neighbor, io-saturation, mitigated

vijay: will draft the postmortem and propose long-term mitigations: tenant admission control, automated io profiles, and cross-pool routing to avoid colocating heavy writers. expected draft by EOD tomorrow.

luke: adding notes to infra backlog: add NVMe write-saturation metric + dashboard, and consider per-tenant IO SLAs

irene: closing thread, will attach logs and exact commands used to the postmortem. good job team :thumbsup:
